meta.label: Mobile carriers
meta.attribution: Curated from public privacy notices, CPNI pages, plan disclosures, terms, coverage pages, and regulator actions. Coverage is local, plans change often, and this is not telecom advice. Check your address and bill terms before switching. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare mobile carriers by privacy, fees, disclosure, and everyday access.

axes.label: Fees or privacy
axes.question: Lower fees or less data exposure?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Tello Mobile
products.description: A highly configurable prepaid carrier for people who want a small bill and can live with MVNO tradeoffs.

privacy.note: Tello publishes privacy rights and opt-out choices, but still collects carrier account, device, usage, and advertising-related data.

fees.note: Tello's custom-plan page shows low-cost build-your-own plans, including very small talk/data plans and low advertised unlimited pricing.

transparency.note: Tello's terms and help pages emphasize no contract, plan changes, and plan limits in plain public pages.

accessibility.note: Tello is online-first and prepaid; that keeps costs low but offers less retail support than national postpaid carriers.

ethics.note: No-contract, change-anytime prepaid service is consumer-friendly, though Tello is not structured around public-interest giving.

products.name: US Mobile
products.description: A flexible MVNO that lets customers choose among multiple network backbones, with many plans showing taxes and fees included.

privacy.note: US Mobile publishes a privacy policy covering account, device, payment, web, and service-use data plus consumer privacy choices.

fees.note: US Mobile's plans page advertises several plans with taxes and fees included, reducing bill-surprise risk.

transparency.note: US Mobile publicly posts terms and plan details, including billing, taxes, and surcharge language.

accessibility.note: US Mobile offers multiple network options, which can help coverage fit, but it remains a mostly online MVNO.

ethics.note: Clear prepaid-style pricing and network choice are consumer-friendly, though the carrier is not a mission-giving provider.

products.name: Visible
products.description: A simple Verizon-owned prepaid option with taxes and fees included, strongest for people who want a low one-line bill on Verizon coverage.

privacy.note: Visible points customers to a privacy policy and choices, but it is Verizon-owned and collects service, web/app, and usage data.

fees.note: Visible's plan pages advertise unlimited service starting at $25 per month with taxes and fees included.

transparency.note: Visible's homepage and plan pages foreground all-in pricing and plan facts, which helps compare the actual monthly bill.

accessibility.note: Visible runs on Verizon's 5G and 4G LTE networks, with broad network access but online-first support.

ethics.note: All-in prepaid pricing is a positive, but Verizon's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the parent company's accountability record.

products.name: Consumer Cellular
products.description: A simple-plan carrier with AARP benefits and phone support, useful for people who value service help over the absolute lowest bill.

privacy.note: Consumer Cellular publishes a privacy and security policy covering personal, device, service, tax, and account data uses.

fees.note: Consumer Cellular advertises no long-term contract and AARP member discounts, but taxes and fees apply to advertised plans.

transparency.note: Consumer Cellular publishes plans and legal/privacy pages, though some bill totals depend on taxes and fees.

accessibility.note: Consumer Cellular's AARP partnership, no long-term contract, and service positioning make it accessible for older adults and support-sensitive users.

ethics.note: The AARP member benefit and senior-friendly service model are public consumer-access positives, with no major 2024 location-data fine found for this MVNO.

products.name: Google Fi Wireless
products.description: A Google-run carrier with strong account integration and travel features, but also a big-platform privacy tradeoff.

privacy.note: Google Fi publishes a Fi-specific privacy page, CPNI explanation, and privacy choices, but it is tied to the wider Google account ecosystem.

fees.note: Google Fi announced a lower-cost Unlimited Essentials plan, but taxes, fees, financing, and add-ons can still affect the bill.

transparency.note: Google Fi provides support pages explaining Fi privacy, CPNI, and account-data controls in one official place.

accessibility.note: Fi is easy for Google-account users and travelers, but local coverage and device compatibility still need address/device checks.

ethics.note: Fi offers useful privacy documentation and some network protections, but dependence on a major ad-tech platform limits public-interest confidence.

products.name: Mint Mobile
products.description: A recognizable prepaid carrier with low promotional prices and bulk-payment savings, now within the T-Mobile orbit.

privacy.note: Mint's privacy policy describes personal, device, account, marketing, and sharing practices rather than a minimal-data carrier model.

fees.note: Mint advertises low monthly prices, but many offers depend on introductory or multi-month prepaid terms and taxes/fees can be extra.

transparency.note: Mint posts plan terms publicly, including limitations, renewal terms, and reduced speeds after high-speed data allotments.

accessibility.note: Mint's online-first prepaid model is easy to buy, but bulk prepayment and coverage fit make it less accessible for some users.

ethics.note: Low prepaid pricing is useful, but T-Mobile's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the ownership family's accountability record.

products.name: Cricket Wireless
products.description: A major prepaid brand with retail presence and taxes-included monthly plan pricing, owned by AT&T.

privacy.note: Cricket's privacy policy says it shares information with AT&T companies and covers advertising, analytics, and account/service data uses.

fees.note: Cricket says monthly plan charges include state and local taxes, which makes many prepaid comparisons easier.

transparency.note: Cricket publicly posts taxes/fees explanations and terms, making the bill structure more inspectable than many postpaid plans.

accessibility.note: Cricket has broad AT&T-network access and retail/prepaid availability, which helps users who want in-person support.

ethics.note: Taxes-included prepaid pricing helps consumers, but AT&T's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the parent company's accountability record.

products.name: Metro by T-Mobile
products.description: A mainstream prepaid brand with taxes and regulatory fees included on many plans, backed by T-Mobile's network.

privacy.note: Metro uses T-Mobile privacy notices and choices, which cover service, device, account, advertising, and CPNI data practices.

fees.note: Metro says applicable taxes and regulatory fees are included in the advertised plan price for its prepaid plans.

transparency.note: Metro publicly explains its taxes-and-fees inclusion and no-contract prepaid positioning.

accessibility.note: Metro combines T-Mobile network access with prepaid retail availability, making it more accessible than online-only MVNOs.

ethics.note: No-contract and taxes-included pricing help, but T-Mobile's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the parent company's accountability record.

products.name: CREDO Mobile
products.description: A mission-oriented mobile provider that turns bills into donations for progressive nonprofits, with a higher-cost tradeoff.

privacy.note: CREDO publishes a privacy policy covering account communications, service data, activism communications, and customer privacy choices.

fees.note: CREDO's mission model is not mainly a low-cost offering; its value claim centers on donations rather than cheapest monthly service.

transparency.note: CREDO publishes donation history and mission pages that make the social-impact claim inspectable.

accessibility.note: CREDO is US-focused and mission-led, but its niche positioning and likely higher bill make it less broadly accessible than budget MVNOs.

ethics.note: CREDO reports more than $95 million donated to progressive nonprofits and lets members vote on monthly donation recipients.

products.name: T-Mobile
products.description: A national carrier with broad access and strong network convenience, but high data exposure and accountability concerns.

privacy.note: T-Mobile's privacy notice covers extensive personal, account, device, location, CPNI, advertising, and sharing practices.

fees.note: T-Mobile's current plan pages state that displayed plan prices can exclude taxes, surcharges, and fees that vary by location.

transparency.note: T-Mobile posts current privacy and plan disclosures, but plan-generation changes and fee exclusions make comparison harder.

accessibility.note: T-Mobile is a national carrier with broad network reach, retail support, and mainstream device/service availability.

ethics.note: The FCC fined T-Mobile more than $80 million in 2024 over illegally sharing access to customer location data.

products.name: Verizon
products.description: A national carrier with broad coverage and retail access, but usually a weaker fit for privacy, fees, and accountability values.

privacy.note: Verizon's privacy policy covers broad collection and use of customer, device, service, advertising, and account data, with privacy choices.

fees.note: Verizon's unlimited-plan pages and surcharge support pages state that taxes, government fees, and Verizon surcharges may be added.

transparency.note: Verizon posts detailed privacy, CPNI, and surcharge pages, but the number of fees and add-ons makes total-price comparison complex.

accessibility.note: Verizon is a national carrier with broad network access, retail support, and mainstream device/service availability.

ethics.note: The FCC fined Verizon almost $47 million in 2024 over illegally sharing access to customer location data.

products.name: AT&T
products.description: A national carrier with broad access and device support, but a weak fit for people optimizing around privacy, fees, and accountability.

privacy.note: AT&T's privacy notice covers wireless, internet, voice, apps, data use, advertising choices, and CPNI-related uses.

fees.note: AT&T's unlimited-plan disclosures say monthly AT&T fees and government taxes are extra, including cost-recovery and other fees.

transparency.note: AT&T publishes privacy and fee schedules, but separate AT&T fees, government taxes, add-ons, and plan changes make bill comparison harder.

accessibility.note: AT&T is a national carrier with broad network access, retail support, and mainstream device/service availability.

ethics.note: The FCC fined AT&T more than $57 million in 2024 over illegally sharing access to customer location data.
